Execution-backed source visual / SPHExampleGPU

StillWedge: the code that actually ran

A top-to-bottom path from the original example to GPU kernels and output. Every code panel is copied literally from the recorded source revision. Expand a function to read its body and helpers; inspect real kernel entries below.

What “precisely” means here

One full 4.00-second invocation was recorded. Only the save directory and the two external-application switches were overridden. The original function body, particle geometry, timestep scheme, physics, GPU flags and 0.01 s output interval were retained. The script's two top-level calls were deliberately not executed.

This is not an instruction-by-instruction GPU debugger. CPU counters identify source instrumentation points that ran. CUPTI identifies GPU kernel entries and their launch geometry. Inlined GPU helpers and per-particle branches do not have device line counters; their full conditional source is shown without inventing line-level execution evidence.

CPU tasks overlap, and CUDA graphs replay without re-running the host wrappers. A kernel may enter and return immediately at a stop guard. Consequently, CPU line hits, GPU kernel entries and accepted physical steps are three different quantities. Recorded timing is instrumented and is not a speed benchmark.

Observed CPU line

Green code rows contain positive process-wide CPU line counters. Amber 0 means an instrumented point had no hit. A dash means no CPU counter, not “never executes”.

Observed kernel entry

Kernel panels show recorded entry counts and exact launch geometry. Code inside an entry still has guards and particle/lane-dependent branches. Device code rows are not falsely colored as covered.

Source / dispatch context

Literal source retains all conditional branches and overloads. Notes identify the selected mode. Unselected overloads remain explicitly available as source context, not observed calls.

01 → 24: linear code path

Read down. An accepted symplectic step is 15 → 16 → 17 → 18 → 19. Stage 20 either requests a rebuild (13), more work (14), or output (21). The layout is logical execution order within one interval, not a claim that concurrent CPU tasks have one global order.

CUPTI device activity

These are actual entries from the complete recording, including guarded no-ops. The seven-kernel step order was verified across all 8,503 attempts, allowing the first/full-state and second/half-state gathers to be labeled separately. Phase labels are source mappings, not device line counters or timestamped CPU call stacks. Click a kernel to open its specific caller context and exact source. Non-package operations are identified as dependency kernels or memory operations.

All reported kernel symbols and entry totals

A count is an entry count, not the number of accepted steps or accepted neighbor pairs. Labels are retained verbatim from CUDA.jl's demangled profiler output; they are not authoritative Julia method signatures. Numeric launch geometry comes directly from the activity records.

Every package subfunction: literal source browser

The original 817-entry package index is included: exported functions, local functions, callbacks, overloads, macros and constructor/type families. Click any entry to open the exact source file at its indexed definition. A source-only entry is not asserted to have executed.
